record.original_question: For G2 Costas arrays constructed over finite fields of characteristic 2, determine the four parity populations ee, eo, oe, and oo, namely the numbers of dots whose coordinates are respectively even-even, even-odd, odd-even, and odd-odd.

evidence.quote: Let ee, eo, oe, and oo stand for the number of dots of the Costas array whose coordinates are both even, even and odd, odd and even, and both odd, respectively: it was found in [40] that, for G2 and W1 arrays, these four quantities, called the parity populations, were not only as equal as they could be.
Problem 17. Determine the parity populations of G2 arrays constructed in fields of characteristic 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let q = 2^k with k ≥ 2, and let F_q be the finite field with q elements. A Costas array of order n is an n × n array containing exactly n dots (one in each row and one in each column) such that the (n choose 2) displacement vectors between distinct pairs of dots are all distinct.

The Golomb (G2) construction over F_q produces a Costas array of order q − 2 as follows. Fix two primitive elements α, β of F_q. For 1 ≤ i, j ≤ q − 2, place a dot at position (i, j) if and only if
   α^i + β^j = 1.
The resulting (q − 2) × (q − 2) array is a Costas array, called a G2 Costas array.

For any Costas array, define its four parity populations
   ee = #{ dots (i, j) : i even and j even },
   eo = #{ dots (i, j) : i even and j odd  },
   oe = #{ dots (i, j) : i odd  and j even },
   oo = #{ dots (i, j) : i odd  and j odd  }.

Problem. For q = 2^k (k ≥ 2), determine, as a function of q and of the choices of primitive elements α, β, the four parity populations ee, eo, oe, oo of the G2 Costas array of order q − 2 constructed above. In particular, give closed-form expressions (or tight characterizations) for these four counts in the characteristic-2 case.
artifact.status_search_result: Web sources on Costas arrays indicate that, while the parity populations of G2 arrays over fields of odd characteristic admit explicit closed forms depending only on q mod 4, the analogous problem in characteristic 2 is known to behave differently (the populations are no longer determined solely by q) and is listed among the unresolved problems in the area. No published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in Costas arrays
status_evidence.snippet: Lists determination of the parity populations of G2 arrays in characteristic 2 as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as open in a survey of Costas-array open problems.

status_evidence.title: Parity properties of Costas arrays defined via finite fields
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes parity-population formulas for G2/Welch arrays in odd characteristic; characteristic-2 case noted as different.
status_evidence.claim: Closed-form parity populations are known in odd characteristic but not in characteristic 2.

status_evidence.title: On some properties of Costas arrays generated via finite fields
status_evidence.snippet: Notes that for G2 with p = 2, parity populations depend on more than just q.
status_evidence.claim: Characteristic-2 G2 parity populations are not determined by q alone, indicating the problem remains nontrivial and unresolved.
